A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LazyEviction. Their complete main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across the substantial experimental expansion and reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original reasoning-benchmark evaluations, attention-pattern observations, memory measurements, and ablations.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations and ablations, including additional domains, model configurations, and decoding-latency measurements.

M1.justification: Section 4 replaces the exponential-plus-reciprocal eviction score with two sigmoid terms, revising the central token-ranking rule. In particular, the printed H2 increases with MRI above 1, whereas v1's reciprocal term decreases. Timestamp/MRI tracking, windowed eviction, and retention of recent tokens remain.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained GSM8K/MATH-500 evaluations and PG-19 diagnostic, v2 adds AIME, GPQA Diamond science questions, LiveCodeBench programming tasks, and a C4 non-reasoning diagnostic. This substantially broadens the evaluated task and domain coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 1–2 add R-KV as an evaluated accuracy comparator while retaining FullKV, H2O, TOVA, and RaaS. Figure 5 retains the original comparator set. RPC is added to related work but is not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: v2 adds Qwen3-4B and QwQ-32B configurations, changes reported window calibration from 50 samples to 1% of test samples, and revises benchmark and ablation budgets. New protocols include a 58-example LiveCodeBench subset and latency/throughput measurements at 4K, 8K, and 16K generation lengths with specified cache budgets.

E4.justification: v2 adds comparisons of alternative score functions, computational-overhead measurements, and the C4 investigation of effectiveness outside reasoning. Existing component, window-size, and threshold ablations are retained and revised; the latter two move to Appendix F. The average-memory/accuracy analyses in v1 Figure 6(b,c) are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the empirical comparisons. Added experiments continue point-estimate reporting; the MRI distributions do not quantify uncertainty in benchmark results.

E6.justification: Accuracy tables and ablation results are extensively replaced and expanded. For Llama-8B on GSM8K, FullKV changes from 74.68 to 81.73 and LazyEviction from 72.70 to 80.06; identical evaluation conditions are not established, so these are not demonstrated same-setting gains. Additional domain/model results and latency measurements appear, while Figure 6(b,c)'s results disappear.

T1.justification: Appendix E.1 adds a computational-complexity argument comparing LazyEviction's O(WB + B log B) overhead per window with repeated ranking by baselines. The attention-error minimization objective and selection formulation from v1 Appendix A.1 are retained in v2 Appendix A.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion broaden the claim from approximately 50% cache reduction on mathematical reasoning to 50–70% reduction across reasoning tasks and models spanning 4B–32B. The conclusion additionally claims performance close to or exceeding FullKV. The central recurring-token contribution remains.

C2.justification: v2 attributes R-KV's cross-domain degradation to its token-similarity assumption and adds an interpretation of runtime overhead. Its C4 findings explicitly restrict the method's advantage to reasoning scenarios. Limitations are substantially revised to discuss offline window calibration and untested larger models, replacing the earlier emphasis on missing non-mathematical evaluations and formal TIR characterization.

D1.justification: v2 supplies an implementation-repository link, benchmark-specific generation limits, thresholds for added models, and model/data source and licensing information. Hardware and software disclosures remain. However, v1's token-length statistics table and explicit average-length-based budget calculation are removed, producing both gains and losses in reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: v2 adds references 37–43, including R-KV, RPC, and additional benchmark/model sources, and contrasts recurrence-based retention with redundancy-based eviction. Scissorhands is reclassified from static retention to cumulative-attention eviction. The broader related-work framework remains.

P1.justification: The main narrative and much of the prose are retained. v2 condenses the abstract and findings, introduces shorter terminology/model names, moves limitations after the conclusion and window/threshold studies to Appendix F, and reorganizes the original appendix subsections.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column layout. Figure 5 is redrawn from four to six panels with compression-ratio axes; Figure 6 retains only its former panel (a). Main comparison tables are rebuilt and expanded, new analysis/runtime tables appear, and the token-length statistics table is removed.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps through broader evaluations, R-KV comparisons, runtime measurements, and clearer applicability limits. However, its revised H2 formula increases with MRI, contradicting the stated preference for smaller MRI; the PDFs do not resolve the implemented scoring rule. Table 1 also contradicts uniform-superiority claims: R-KV wins two GSM8K columns. These evidential gains and newly introduced method/claim inconsistencies prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
